Inside WIRED’s Secret Interview with Nathan Fielder

WIRED’s global editorial director, Katie Drummond, recently discussed her extensive, highly guarded interview with comedian and filmmaker Nathan Fielder regarding his secret new documentary, You Can See Everything. The project, co-directed with Lance Oppenheim, follows Fielder spending a month inside the home of Elizabeth Holmes during the weeks before she began her prison sentence for defrauding investors through Theranos.

Kept under wraps for three years with only a few dozen people seeing it prior to its debut at the Telluride Film Festival, the film presented unique hurdles for editors. Drummond recounted how she initially received an obscure email from Fielder's publicist and had to sign a nondescript non-disclosure agreement before even knowing the project was a film. During their hour-and-a-half conversation, Fielder—who is notoriously reluctant to participate in press interviews—frequently turned the tables to ask Drummond about her own perspectives on the movie.

Alongside the interview release, former WIRED editor Adam Rogers published a retrospective examining the magazine's early 2010s coverage of Theranos. Drummond noted that the piece serves as a sharp editorial reckoning, highlighting how media culture at the time tended to lionize young startup founders and disruptive tech narratives without applying the stringent skepticism common today.

Tech Billionaires Announce Sudden Philanthropic Pledges

In the same media cycle, recent announcements from major tech figures have sparked discussions regarding corporate philanthropy and artificial intelligence. Anthropic announced it would commit 5 percent of its company shares to a public benefit fund intended to help address the labor market impacts of AI. Shortly afterward, Elon Musk posted on X that he plans to give a SpaceX share to every child in America next year as the first of multiple distributions.

Commentators have noted the vague nature of these announcements. Anthropic's fund could potentially direct money or donations toward "specific populations," while Musk's proposal lacked specific logistical details. Observers link these sudden gestures to a shifting public relations landscape as AI companies face rising scrutiny over energy demands, data centers, and potential job displacement.

Practical Implications & Verification

  • What is Confirmed: Katie Drummond conducted a long-form interview with Nathan Fielder regarding You Can See Everything, which explores his time inside Elizabeth Holmes' home prior to her imprisonment. Anthropic formally stated its intention to allocate 5 percent of its shares to a public benefit fund, and Elon Musk posted about distributing SpaceX shares to children. WIRED also reported that election offices across at least 32 states received suspicious letters, some containing white powder.
  • What Remains Uncertain: Specific implementation details, timelines, and regulatory feasibility for both Anthropic's fund and Musk's share distribution plan remain largely undefined.
  • How to Check: Readers can verify the original reporting, podcast audio, and related articles directly through the [WIRED Official Source](https://www.wired.com/story/uncanny-valley-podcast-inside-the-secret-nathan-fielder-interview/).
